Managua]]|}} }} '''Holdyn Jerian Grant''' (born October 9, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] (GBL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played college basketball with the [[University of Notre Dame]] and was considered one of the top college players in the nation for the [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15 season]]. After being selected with the 19th overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]], his rights were sent to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] and then moved to the [[New York Knicks]] on draft night. Grant is widely considered as one of the best defenders in the EuroLeague.{{cite web | title=Jerian Grant embraces lockdown defender role, compares EuroLeague's top guards | url=https://basketnews.com/news-200147-jerian-grant-embraces-lockdown-defender-role-compares-euroleagues-top-guards.html }} ==College career== After a high school career at prep power [[DeMatha Catholic High School]], Grant came to Notre Dame to play for coach [[Mike Brey]]. After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] his freshman season,{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Dauster|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/11/13/the-maturation-jerian-grant-what-one-star-learned-during-a-season-long-suspension/|title=The maturation of Jerian Grant: What one star learned during a season-long suspension|work=NBCSports.com|date=November 13, 2014|access-date=February 1, 2015}} Grant was named to the [[Big East Conference]] All-Rookie team after averaging 12.3 points and 4.97 assists per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.und.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030412aaa.html|title=Jack Cooley And Jerian Grant Named To BIG EAST All-Conference Teams|work=UND.com|date=March 4, 2012|access-date=February 1, 2015}} In his second season with the Irish, Grant was named second-team All-Big East after averaging 13.3 points and 5.5 assists per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.csnchicago.com/blog/irish-talk/cooley-grant-named-all-big-east-teams |title=Cooley, Grant named to All-Big East teams |work=[[Comcast SportsNet Chicago]] |date=March 10, 2013 |access-date=February 1, 2015 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304055034/http://www.csnchicago.com/blog/irish-talk/cooley-grant-named-all-big-east-teams |archive-date=March 4, 2016 }} After the 2012–13 season, Notre Dame moved from the Big East to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). Based on his strong sophomore campaign, Grant was voted onto the preseason All-ACC team.{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Murray|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/10/syracuse_forward_cj_fair_voted.html|title=Syracuse's C.J. Fair voted ACC preseason player of the year; Orange picked to finish 2nd in league|work=Syracuse.com|date=March 10, 2013|access-date=February 1, 2015}} Grant had a strong start to the season, leading the Fighting Irish at 19.01 points per game during their 8–4 start. But on December 23, 2013, Grant was ruled academically ineligible for the rest of the season and forced to withdraw from Notre Dame.{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Fortuna|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10182486/academics-force-notre-dame-fighting-irish-leading-scorer-jerian-grant-leave-team|title=Notre Dame Loses Leading Scorer|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2013|access-date=February 1, 2015}} Grant chose to return to Notre Dame rather than declare his eligibility for the [[2014 NBA draft]].{{cite magazine|first=Brian|last=Hamilton|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2014/09/04/jerian-grant-notre-dame-acc-suspension|title=Jerian Grant returns from suspension to make Notre Dame relevant again|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=September 4, 2014|access-date=February 1, 2015}} Grant returned to Notre Dame for the 2014–15 season. Grant immediately helped the Fighting Irish to a 20–3 start and Grant personally had a breakout season as the leader of the team's highly efficient offense.{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Dauster|url=http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/01/29/film-session-the-case-for-jerian-grant-as-national-player-of-the-year/|title=Film Session: The case for Jerian Grant as National Player of the Year|work=NBCSports.com|date=January 29, 2015|access-date=February 1, 2015}} He was named to the midseason watch lists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]] and the [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]].{{cite news|first=Nick|last=Erickson|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/early-lead/wp/2015/01/14/wooden-award-midseason-top-25-list-revealed/|title=Wooden Award Midseason Top 25 list revealed|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|date=January 14, 2015|access-date=February 1, 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2015/oscar150123.html|title=Oscar Robertson Trophy Midseason Watch List Announced|work=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]]|date=January 23, 2015|access-date=February 1, 2015}} The Grant-led Irish finished the year with a 32–6 record and an ACC Tournament championship; they advanced to the Elite 8 in the Midwest Region, where they lost to an undefeated Kentucky team by 2 points.{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Withers|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/survived-no-1-kentucky-holds-off-notre-dame-031309800--ncaab.html|title=Survived No. 1 Kentucky holds off Notre Dame 68–66|work=Yahoo.com|date=March 28, 2015|access-date=March 28, 2015|archive-date=December 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220230133/https://sports.yahoo.com/news/survived-no-1-kentucky-holds-off-notre-dame-031309800--ncaab.html|url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== ===New York Knicks (2015–2016)=== [[File:Jerian Grant 2015.jpg|thumb|right|Grant dribbles the ball in 2015]] Grant was selected the 19th overall pick by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2015 NBA draft]]. His rights were subsequently traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] before finally being traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Tim Hardaway Jr.]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/draft/knicks-acquire-draft-rights-jerian-grant|title=Knicks Acquire Draft Rights To Jerian Grant|date=June 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 26, 2015}} He later would be joining his older brother, [[Jerai Grant|Jerai]]. In 27 games in the [[Greek Basket League]], Grant averaged 14.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 6.7 assists. ===Olimpia Milano (2021–2022)=== [[File:2021-12-03 ALBA Berlin gegen Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano (EuroLeague 2021-22) by Sandro Halank–014.jpg|thumb|right|Grant warms up before a game in 2021]] On July 1, 2021, Grant officially signed a two-year deal with [[Olimpia Milano]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]], under coach [[Ettore Messina]].{{cite news |title=Jerian Grant officially signs a two-year deal with Olimpia Milano |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jerian-grant-officially-signs-a-two-year-deal-with-olimpia-milano/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 1, 2021 |date=July 1, 2021}} On July 2, 2022, he parted ways with the Italian club, having won both domestic titles during his stint. ===Türk Telekom (2022–2023)=== On July 14, 2022, Grant signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketfaul.com/haber?haber=102223|title=Telekom'a NBA patentli guard|last=|first=|date=July 14, 2022|website=|publisher=basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=August 5, 2022}} In the domestic league, he averaged 16.4 points, 3.6 rebounds and 5.7 assists per game, leading the club to the 1st place in the regular season standings. Additionally, in 22 [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] matches, he averaged 14.9 points, 3.2 rebounds, 6.1 assists and 1.3 steals in 33 minutes per contest, and reached the final with his team, where they were defeated by [[CB Gran Canaria]]. For these efforts, Grant was named Most Valuable Player of the [[2022–23 EuroCup Basketball|2022–2023 EuroCup season]]. ===Panathinaikos (2023–present)=== On July 10, 2023, Grant signed a one-year contract with Greek powerhouse [[Panathinaikos B.C.]].{{cite web |title=Jerian Grant officially joins Panathinaikos |url=https://basketnews.com/news-191849-jerian-grant-officially-joins-panathinaikos.html |website=BasketNews.com |date=10 July 2023 |access-date=19 August 2025}} On July 10, 2024, Grant renewed his contract for an additional two seasons, keeping him with the club until the end of the 2025–26 season.{{cite web |title=Jerian Grant renews at Panathinaikos until 2026 |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/jerian-grant-renews-at-panathinaikos-bc-until-2026/ |website=EuroLeague.net |date=10 July 2024 |access-date=19 August 2025}} On June 14, 2025, Grant signed a further contract extension with improved terms through 2028, solidifying his role as a key contributor to the team's success.{{cite web |title=Panathinaikos extends Jerian Grant through 2028 |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/panathinaikos-extends-jerian-grant-through-2028/ |website=EuroLeague.net |date=14 June 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}} During his time at Panathinaikos, Grant has been instrumental in the team's achievements, including winning the EuroLeague title in the 2023–24 season. In the championship game against [[Real Madrid]], he delivered an all-around performance, contributing 11 points, six rebounds, five assists, two steals, and a performance index rating (PIR) of 17.{{cite web |title=Panathinaikos extends Jerian Grant through 2028 |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/panathinaikos-extends-jerian-grant-through-2028/ |website=EuroLeague.net |date=14 June 2025 |access-date=19 August 2025}} Grant's consistent performance and leadership on both ends of the court have made him a fan favorite at [[OAKA Basketball Arena]], with his contract Jerian Grant is the son of former [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) player [[Harvey Grant]]. He has three brothers, two of whom play basketball professionally – his older brother [[Jerai Grant|Jerai]] has played in several leagues around the world and his younger brother [[Jerami Grant|Jerami]] plays for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. His youngest brother Jaelin also played basketball at DeMatha. His uncle and father's identical twin [[Horace Grant]] was an [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and won four championships with the [[Chicago Bulls]] and [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite
